Quick update from SLA ops: I replayed the service probes and the edge telemetry for the timeframe. Observations:
- Redwood probe fleet registered elevated p50/p95 latency starting at 01:47:30 UTC with sporadic request timeouts; the probe failure rate peaked at ~6.7% between 01:55–02:12 UTC.
- Backend host metrics (GPU pool) show no scheduled maintenance during the window.
- We observed elevated error rates on a small subset of POPs in the us-west region; preliminary traceroutes show a mid-path ASN change consistent with CDN routing instability.

Interpretation so far: the ledger classifies this as a partial-degradation window (we internally call these "penumbra" windows when degradation is spread across probes and not a full outage). Under our SLA wording, if a third-party CDN caused an upstream routing flap and the customer traffic was affected via our edge, we have to apportion eligibility carefully — sometimes we exclude third-party upstreams if the failure is fully outside our control, but if our edge failed to failover within the SLO, it counts toward the ledger.

Ask for Solum: can you provide the customer telemetry slice (errors by POP) and any CDN-side logs you have so we can correlate and identify whether Redwood failed to fail over within the configured timeout.

I'll begin a ledger recalculation using the probe weighting rule and include per-POP breakdown. Expect a results email in ~18 hours.

Michael —

Thank you for the CDN incident link and the extra telemetry. Kimberly's team completed the ledger recalculation this afternoon. High-level summary:
- Ledger shows a 42-minute partial-degradation window (01:47:30–02:29:30 UTC) weighted by probe visibility.
- Apportionment model attributes ~63% of the degradation to the CDN routing flap and ~37% to an edge failover delay where our edge took ~35s longer than target to switch routes to an alternate POP.

Per the contract (section 3.2, routing & upstream exclusions), Redwood excludes third-party upstream outages only when there is a clean handoff and no observable delay in our failover. Because we measured a failover delay above the internal SLO in one POP cluster, we cannot fully exclude the entire window.

Proposed remediation:
1) We can offer a provisional credit equal to the apportioned customer-impact: 37% of the credit calculated for the 42-minute window. That equates to a provisional one-off credit of 0.37 * (monthly per-SLA formula).
2) Open a postmortem with engineering and the CDN partner to tighten our failover path; we'll share a timeline and mitigation plan within 10 business days.
3) If Solum provides evidence that the CDN incident caused the specific edge failure (packet traces showing TCP reset chain originating upstream), and engineering confirms the edge would have failed regardless, we'll revisit and potentially increase exclusion to 100%.

Please confirm whether you accept the provisional credit so Marissa can prepare the adjustment.
